## Explanations

### Recap: the puff of air

No new sounds today. You've met six pairs that differ only in a **puff of air**: the second of each pair has one, the first doesn't.

Hand in front of your mouth: b d g z zh j stay still, p t k c ch q blow. This lesson mixes them all up, in all four tones.

**bō** · **pō**  
**dè** · **tè**  
**gē** · **kē**  
**zè** · **cè**  
**zhē** · **chē** (vehicle, car)  
**jī** · **qī** (seven)  

### Puff or no puff

Three pairs in all four tones: without a puff, then with one.

| | 1st tone | 2nd tone | 3rd tone | 4th tone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ge** | gē | gé | gě | gè |
| **ke** | kē | ké | kě | kè |
| **ze** | zē | zé | zě | zè |
| **ce** | cē | cé | cě | cè |
| **ji** | jī | jí | jǐ | jì |
| **qi** | qī | qí | qǐ | qì |

### Puff and tone together

Now both at once: which initial, and which tone? Take your time: listen to the start for the puff, then to the pitch.

**gē** · **ké** · **gě** · **kè**  
**jī** · **qí** · **jǐ** (how many?) · **qì**  

### kě, kè, kè

Three words start with **k**: **kě** (thirsty), **kè** (class) and **kèqi** (polite), and **kělè** starts with kě. Listen for the tone of the first syllable: low, or falling?

**kě** (thirsty) · **kělè** (cola)  
**kè** (class, lesson) · **kèqi** (polite)  

## New words

| Pinyin | Meaning | Note |
|--------|---------|------|
| **kělè**<br><sub>ke3le4</sub> | cola | A puff on the k, none on the l. Low, then falling. Literally: can + happy. |
| **kèqi**<br><sub>ke4qi5</sub> | polite | qi is light here. Later: bú kèqi, you're welcome (literally: don't be polite). |

## New phrases

| Pinyin | English | Literally |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| **Wǒ hē kělè.**<br><sub>Wo3 he1 ke3le4.</sub> | I'll have a cola. / I drink cola. | I / drink / cola |
| **Gēge kèqi.**<br><sub>Ge1ge5 ke4qi5.</sub> | My brother is polite. | older brother / polite |

**hē** (to drink), **kě** (thirsty), **gēge** (older brother), **Wǒ kě le.** (I'm thirsty (now).), **Wǒ hé gēge** (me and my older brother), **kè** (class, lesson), **Zhège ne?** (And this one? / What about this one?), **qìchē** (automobile, car), **Wǒ xǐ chē.** (I'm washing the car.)
